messages:
viv: FYI customer B asked for a scoped export for a security review: all req/resp pairs for their tenant over a 3-day period, including attachments. They want a csv of metadata + the payloads. How can we do that and still keep PII safe?

cheng: We should avoid handing over raw payloads unless absolutely necessary. Options: 1) produce a redacted export based on confidence thresholds, 2) provide an encrypted forensic bundle with strict access controls, or 3) provide pseudonymized artifacts + linkage keys for lawful requests.

soham: Agree. Practical flow: default export = redacted+fingerprints. If customer requests provenance (unredacted) we require explicit legal auth plus a temporary unmask token. Store unredacted material only encrypted with per-tenant KMS and auto-expire.

viv: Two follow-ups: how do we handle attachments (images/pdf) and embeddings? We can't store raw embeddings as-is for export.

cheng: For attachments: compute an HMAC and a content type fingerprint, strip binary, keep name/size/mimetype. For images where OCR runs, store OCR text redacted using PII detectors and confidence scores. For embeddings: store a signed bloom filter or truncated hash of the vector that preserves matchability but not reconstructability.

soham: We also need a redaction confidence score per field. Console export UI should show fields flagged with low confidence and allow reviewers to request a deeper review. But deeper review requires legal workflow.

jena-legal: Legal: must require a justification string, owner approver, and a legal sign-off step before any unredacted data is released. Retention for any unredacted export should be <= 30 days by default. Also maintain immutable access logs with the requester's identity and IP.

viv: UX idea: add a two-step export button in the console: "Prepare export (redacted)" -> shows cost estimate, sample preview, fields redacted + confidence -> "Request unredact" that kicks off approval flow. Show estimated token burn and storage size.

soham: Minimal API for automation:
```
POST /internal/exports/create
{
  "tenant_id": "t-789",
  "start_ts": 6080000000,
  "end_ts": 6080250000,
  "redaction_profile": "high-confidence",
  "attachment_strategy": "hmac+ocr",
  "embedding_strategy": "bf-signature",
  "sample_rate": 0.02
}
```
Then PATCH to request unredact with approver ticket id.

cheng: Backend: exports run on a sidepath worker with rate-limited read tokens. Documents go to a tenant-scoped encrypted bucket with metadata index. Exports should annotate each record with redact_reason and redaction_confidence. We should also compute quick diffs so repeated exports are delta-only.

viv: Ops-bot: any perf impact alerts for running exports?

ops-bot: heads-up: heavy export workloads can saturate read throughput. Recommend placing quota of 5 concurrent exports per org and default sample_rate=0.01 for self-serve. Canary scheduled for 2% of traffic this weekend.

soham: One more: searchability. If we HMAC attachments we should provide a search API that can ingest a probe file and return matching HMACs so investigators can check presence without seeing content. Document the key rotation policy so HMACs remain valid for the forensic window.

jena-legal: Also request an audit mode that masks user ids but preserves transaction ids for mapping. And keep a legal-only key escrow for emergencies.

viv: Good notes. I'll write a short RFC covering: console two-step export UX, API surface, HMAC/fingerprint strategies for attachments and embeddings, confidence-based redaction, retention/TTL, KMS patterns, approval flow, and quotas. Will tag infra + security + legal for review.

ops-bot: Note: RFC review meeting scheduled Fri 15:00 UTC.

viv: Thanks — will drop RFC link here once ready. :white_check_mark:
